transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-09-15, Time: 16:00 PDT - 16:47 PDT; Duration: ~47 minutes; Location: Zoom; Recording: yes; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Renee Patel (Trillium Procurement), Victor Huang (Trillium Security), Lena Morales (Trillium Legal)

Summary: Quick procurement + legal sync to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA/latency expectations for a pilot, and privileged keying/KMS options. Customer concerned about data residency, KMS/HSM, and pricing variability for burst traffic. Redwood walked through hosting modes and a pricing path with reserve vs burst.

Topics: MSA/DPA exceptions, SOC2 and audit deliverables, KMS integration and privilege model, SLA latency thresholds, pricing scenarios (on-demand vs committed), next-step pilot kickoff and technical checklist.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood. Diego, you want to intro quickly?
[00:08] Diego Alvarez: Yeah hi, Diego here, SE. We'll cover connectivity, KMS, and the quick cost tradeoffs.
[00:14] Renee Patel: Thanks, we only have 45, so want to focus on approvals. We need to understand the commercial path and if you support our key management rules.
[00:24] Victor Huang: And security: SOC2, audit logs, and whether keys leave our control — that's an absolute blocker for us.
[00:32] Lena Morales: A couple legal points on the DPA, mostly around subprocessors and data deletion timelines.
[00:39] Maya Chen: Totally. High level: Redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private. For regulated PHI-ish workloads, most customers pick Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS. But for pilot we typically support a hosted sandbox with strict egress controls.
[00:55] Diego Alvarez: Quick clarification — our Dedicated pools can be VPC peered, or we can do Private where the control plane is customer-managed. KMS options: bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM or Redwood-managed with strict RBAC.
[01:12] Victor Huang: When you say KMS, do you have an HSM-backed flow? We need FIPS 140-2 equivalence, and logs of every key access. Also we want to ensure the key never leaves our region.
[01:24] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can integrate with major cloud KMS providers and some HSM partners. Key material doesn't leave the KMS — we do envelope encryption and the KV cache is stored encrypted. I might have said K-V cash earlier in a demo, sorry for the slur — it should be K-V cache.
[01:40] Lena Morales: On the DPA, our standard asks for 30-day deletion window after contract termination, and subprocessors list. Can you accept that?
[01:48] Maya Chen: We can accept a 30-day reasonable deletion clause; subprocessors we provide a maintained list and can include a notice clause with exception handling. There are standard carve-outs for managed infra providers.
[02:01] Renee Patel: Pricing — show us committed vs on-demand. We have bursty traffic due to batches of EMR ingest. If we commit too much it's wasted; if we go on-demand, costs spike.
[02:14] Diego Alvarez: Right, common. Our recommendation is a small committed baseline for predictable low-latency paths and a burst tier that's metered. We also recommend prefix K-V caching to lower token costs for repeated prompts.
[02:28] Victor Huang: Latency targets — we need 95th percentile under 250ms for the main inference route. Is that realistic on hosted?
[02:36] Diego Alvarez: On hosted globally it's tight for that SLA unless you use Dedicated pools in-region. For 250ms 95p you'd want Dedicated capacity in your primary region or Private deployment near your VPC. Otherwise we can route to the regional edge but there's more variance.
[02:50] Maya Chen: Also, we can do an SLA addendum for Dedicated customers with uptime and latency SLOs. For proof of concept we usually provide an operational readout and SLA proposal for the commitment stage.
[03:03] Lena Morales: Regarding indemnities and data risk: our legal team wants to cap subprocessors to pre-approved vendors and have audit right clauses. How do you handle that?
[03:13] Maya Chen: We have a subprocessors appendix; for enterprise we can agree to a list and a notification window. Audit rights are scoped — we provide SOC2 reports and can do an on-site or desktop audit in exceptional cases.
[03:25] Victor Huang: Can you anonymize logs for audit? We need to ensure PHI isn't present.
[03:31] Diego Alvarez: Yes, customers can opt into token redaction and trimmed logs. There's a cost/visibility tradeoff; you lose some debugging telemetry but gain compliance posture.
[03:44] Renee Patel: Procurement question — will you accept a PO first for pilot and then commercial contract?
[03:50] Maya Chen: Yes many customers start with an initial PO + SOW for pilot and then move to a Master Service Agreement with MSA and DPA in parallel. We'll coordinate legal routing.
[03:59] Renee Patel: Good, that helps internal timelines. We have a pricing committee that needs committed spend options.
[04:06] Diego Alvarez: For the pricing committee we can present three scenarios: conservative committed baseline, medium commit + burst buffer, and pure on-demand. We'll include estimated egress and storage for your ingest patterns.
[04:20] Lena Morales: On DPA retention, what about backups and geo-redundant copies? We need data kept only in the US for now.
[04:29] Diego Alvarez: We can configure region pins on Dedicated and Private so data rests in the US region. For hosted variants we can pin model routing to US, but some telemetry might touch other regions for infra — which we can avoid if you require strictly US-only.
[04:42] Victor Huang: Encryption keys for backups — same KMS?
[04:45] Diego Alvarez: Yes same KMS envelope flow. Backups encrypted with customer KMS when BYOK is used.
[04:49] Maya Chen: Quick note about model fallbacks: we surface model variants and you can pin versions. If the primary model is unavailable we can fallback to a compatible variant but we mark that in logs and you can require autoswitch off if that's not acceptable.
[05:05] Renee Patel: Hmm, fallback is fine for non-critical flows but not for regulated outputs.
[05:09] Diego Alvarez: Understood. We can set per-route policies: strict route (no fallback) for regulated endpoints and flexible for others.
[05:19] Lena Morales: Contract redlines — our legal team will propose three small MSA changes: 1) stronger data deletion language, 2) audit rights window, 3) a clear SLA credit schedule. Any immediate concerns?
[05:31] Maya Chen: None of those are showstoppers. SLA credits we can sign off in the Dedicated proposal; audit windows we usually negotiate the scope. We'll flag the data deletion phrasing to legal.
[05:42] Victor Huang: There's also the KMS provider preference — we use CloudKeyX as our standard. Do you see issues integrating?
[05:47] Diego Alvarez: We haven't worked with CloudKeyX directly but our BYOK layer is provider-agnostic for standard KMS APIs. There's sometimes a connector work item; we can plan a short integration spike in pilot.
[05:58] Renee Patel: On procurement timing — if we get pricing and MSA redlines this week, what's a realistic start date for pilot?
[06:05] Maya Chen: If approvals move quickly, pilot could start ~2 weeks after contract signature. So end of month timeline is plausible.
[06:12] Diego Alvarez: For the pilot technical checklist: VPC peering, KMS test keys, sample dataset for throughput benchmarks, and a latency SLA target. We'll also run a short benchmark to validate the 95p latency.
[06:25] Victor Huang: We'll need the benchmark infra to reflect our traffic shapes — mostly spikes during nightly batches.
[06:31] Diego Alvarez: We'll use replay scripts and can do load with realistic sequence lengths. Also we'll test prefix caching impact.
[06:42] Lena Morales: A quick note on subprocessors — any third-party monitoring agents or tracing services? We prefer those to be optional.
[06:50] Maya Chen: Tracing is optional. We can disable third-party telemetry for your tenant; logs can be shipped to your SIEM instead.
[06:58] Renee Patel: Can you provide a sample SOW for the pilot? Need scoping for deliverables.
[07:03] Maya Chen: Yes we'll include SOW scope in the pricing deck.
[07:08] Diego Alvarez: One more technical caveat — quantization and model selection can change token cost and latency tradeoffs. We'll include recommended quantization profiles per workload.
[07:20] Victor Huang: If we go with quantized models, do we lose support for certain plugins or function-calling?
[07:26] Diego Alvarez: Some advanced ops are model-dependent; function calling is supported broadly but some precision-sensitive outputs prefer full precision. We'll list feature compat matrix.
[07:37] Lena Morales: Okay, on the legal side we'll send redlines to Maya. Expect our redlines for MSA + DPA by EOD Friday.
[07:45] Renee Patel: Procurement will confirm whether we'll do PO-first.
[07:49] Maya Chen: Recap: I'll send pricing deck + three commitment scenarios; Diego will share SOC2 and KMS integration notes and a VPC diagram; Trillium will return MSA/DPA redlines and procurement decision. We'll aim to reconvene after your redlines and pricing review.
[08:07] Victor Huang: One last quick ask: can you include a short note on incident response — escalation contacts and RTOs?
[08:15] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll include incident response playbook excerpt.
[08:19] Lena Morales: Good. That should be enough for now.
[08:23] Maya Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[08:28] Renee Patel: Thanks, bye.
[08:30] (meeting ends)
